questions: Is the five-sensor span of 0.06 m with 12 mm footprints enough to give a usable, non-saturated signal on every development track?
Does the 0.05 m forward sensor offset cause lag or oscillation at the controller level, or is it a benefit?
Is the mass of 0.7 kg and wheel track of 0.12 m responsive enough for the slalom, or does turning look sluggish?
Are there any points where the sum of readings drops near the 0.05 line-loss threshold, and on which track?

intent: Establish a symmetric five-sensor baseline with a 0.06 m span and a forward offset of 0.05 m, mid-range drivetrain, and light mass. The aim is to see whether this platform completes all development tracks with few line losses and a fast completion time. The Integrator should report whether the sensor spacing is too coarse or too fine for a controller to use, and whether the forward offset adds lag.
learning: No prior races, so these are hypotheses to test. H1: the wide sensor span reduces line-loss events. H2: a forward offset of about 0.05 m improves bend anticipation without adding oscillation. H3: a light body with a mid-range wheel track gives enough turn authority for the slalom. Next, I want the measurements to show line-loss counts, max and RMS error per track, and steering oscillation, so I can tell whether the span and offset or the drivetrain is limiting the score.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or integration feedback yet. The design therefore starts from the contract's limits and sound priors. Five sensors spread across the front of the body at x = +0.03, +0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03 with 12 mm footprints give a 0.06 m sensing span. The tape is 25 mm wide, so the sensors overlap enough that the line stays visible through modest lateral error. The wide span also keeps the sum of readings above the 0.05 line-loss threshold when the robot drifts. The sensors sit 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the signal is read before the wheels turn, which helps the controller respond to bends. The body is 0.12 m wide, which gives an off-track limit of 0.06 m, the floor value, and is wide enough to avoid a tight body constraint. The wheel track is 0.12 m and the wheel radius 0.03 m, a mid-range drivetrain that should allow a fast average speed, with the 3 s deadline requiring roughly 1.5 m/s. Mass is 0.7 kg, a light robot that accelerates quickly while keeping the yaw inertia low, since mass times (length squared plus width squared)/12 governs how fast it can turn. I expect a first race to complete the oval with few line losses. The main unknowns are whether the sensor span is too wide for the slalom's sharpest bends and whether the 0.05 m forward offset causes lag. Both should show up in the measurements requested below.
